Cautiously positive overall. The FOMC statement cites strengthening activity, solid job gains, and accommodative financial conditions despite elevated inflation and virus-related risks. SLOOS evidence reinforces this positive tilt on the credit channel: banks broadly eased standards for C&I and CRE loans and reported stronger business loan demand across large, middle-market, and small firms, with increased credit line inquiries and investment-driven needs—supportive of continued growth. Offsetting factors include SLOOS-reported weaker demand for residential real estate loans and expectations of deterioration in household credit (credit card, auto, and nonconforming jumbo), alongside anticipated rate increases. These headwinds, together with financial stability vulnerabilities noted around the period, temper the outlook. Net effect: positive but moderated, slightly stronger than baseline due to easier business credit conditions.
